channel.title: Mister Translation
channel.description: A fresh translation of the Bible into modern English, made from the original Hebrew and Greek one chapter at a time.

item.title: Ephesians 3
item.description: “For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus —” and the sentence breaks off for twelve verses while Paul explains the mystery he was given to steward: that the nations are co-heirs, co-members of one body and co-sharers of the promise. ⚠ He calls himself “less than…

item.title: Galatians 6
item.description: The last chapter of Galatians turns from argument to the congregation: mend the one caught in a trespass, “bear one another’s burdens, and so you will fulfill the law of Christ,” yet each one carries his own load, two different Greek words. God is not mocked; whatever a…

item.title: Galatians 5
item.description: “For freedom Christ set us free”: the chapter turns the allegory of Hagar and Sarah into a command not to take up a yoke of slavery again. ⚠ Circumcision as the doorway to the whole law, “released from Christ,” “fallen from grace,” and faith working through love; a race…

item.title: Galatians 4
item.description: The heir who is a minor, no different from a slave, under guardians and stewards until the date his father set; ⚠ “the elements of the world,” a word that can mean the ABCs, the stuff of matter, or the powers behind the stars; and “when the fullness of the time came,” a Son…

item.title: Galatians 3
item.description: “O senseless Galatians, who has put the evil eye on you?” Paul asks one question twice: did you receive the Spirit by works of law, or by the hearing of faith? Then Abraham, who “believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness,” and a chain of quotations that Paul…

item.title: Galatians 2
item.description: Fourteen years later Paul goes up to Jerusalem again, with Barnabas and with Titus, an uncircumcised Greek, and lays his gospel before “those who seemed important.” Titus is not compelled to be circumcised; false brothers “smuggled in” to spy out the freedom are not given an…

item.title: 2 Corinthians 13
item.description: The letter ends with a warning and a blessing. Paul is coming a third time, and he quotes the law of witnesses — “at the mouth of two witnesses and of three every matter shall stand” — to say that this time he will not spare. The Corinthians want proof that Christ speaks in…

item.title: Joshua 24
item.description: Joshua gathers the tribes at Shechem, recites what God has done from Terah to the Amorites, and sets the choice before them: serve Jehovah, or the gods beyond the River or of the Amorites. The people answer that they will serve Jehovah. He makes a covenant, writes the law and…

item.title: Joshua 23
item.description: Joshua, old and near death, calls the elders, heads, judges and officers of Israel and reminds them that Jehovah fought for them. He warns that if they cleave to the remaining nations, intermarry with them and serve their gods, the land itself will be lost; every promise has…

item.title: Joshua 22
item.description: Joshua 22 sends the eastern tribes home. Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh cross the Jordan with their share of the spoil, then build a great altar by the river. Israel hears of it, gathers at Shiloh for war, and sends Phinehas and ten chiefs to ask what treachery this is.…

item.title: Joshua 21
item.description: Joshua 21 gives the Levites their forty-eight cities by lot: thirteen for the priests from Judah, Simeon and Benjamin, ten for the rest of Kohath, thirteen for Gershon, twelve for Merari. The Masoretic text drops two verses, the four cities of Reuben, so the chapter’s count…

item.title: Romans 16
item.description: “I commend to you Phoebe, our sister” — and then the longest list of names in the letter. Phoebe, a servant of the congregation at Cenchreae, probably carries it; Prisca and Aquila, who risked their necks; Junia, “outstanding among the apostles”; and more than two dozen…

item.title: Romans 15
item.description: “We who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak.” The strong carry the load of the weak, and Christ is the model: he did not please himself. Three quotations in three verses, from the Law, the Psalms and the Prophets, make the case that the nations belong to the…

item.title: Romans 14
item.description: “Welcome the one who is weak in faith” — the chapter on the weak and the strong. The letter answers the dispute over food and days with one sentence about the kingdom: it is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the holy spirit. ⚠ Every person stands…

item.title: Romans 13
item.description: “Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities” — the sentence the state has quoted for two thousand years, and that its critics have quoted back at it ever since. ⚠ Every authority is placed in order by God, the one who sets himself against that order has opposed…

item.title: Romans 12
item.description: After the mercies of chapter 11, the letter turns to the practical half. “I urge you, then, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice” — a reasonable service, not a ritual, and an instruction not to be shaped by this age but transformed by…

item.title: Romans 11
item.description: “I say, then, God has not pushed away his people, has he? May it never be! For I too am an Israelite, from the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” After the last verse of chapter 10 (“All day long I spread out my hands to a disobedient and contradicting people”)…

item.title: Joshua 20
item.description: Jehovah speaks to Joshua for the last time in this book, in a sentence found nowhere else, and what he says is Numbers 35 with Moses’ name replaced: give for yourselves the cities of refuge. The man they protect is described with two phrases the older laws kept apart, BY…

item.title: Romans 7
item.description: “Or do you not know, brothers … that the law is lord over a man for as long as he lives?” Chapter 6 ended with the law standing at its edge (“you are not under law but under grace”), and chapter 7 takes it up with a picture from marriage law: a woman is bound to her husband…

item.title: Romans 10
item.description: “Brothers, the goodwill of my heart and my petition to God on their behalf are indeed for salvation.” After the stone of stumbling at the end of chapter 9, chapter 10 begins with a wish, a petition and a diagnosis: Israel has “a zeal for God, but not according to accurate…

item.title: Joshua 19
item.description: The other six lots come out in order. Simeon’s falls inside Judah’s own share, with thirteen cities counted and fourteen named, most of them towns Judah’s lists already hold. Zebulun’s border goes up ‘westward’ in a word that also means ‘to the sea,’ and passes Jonah’s town.…

item.title: Joshua 18
item.description: The congregation gathers at Shiloh and settles the tent of meeting, the land at last ‘subdued’ as Moses told Reuben and Gad it would have to be — and Joshua asks the seven tribes still without land how long they will go slack, the same root Pharaoh once turned on Israel.…

item.title: Romans 9
item.description: “I am telling the truth in Christ, I am not lying … I could pray to be, I myself, accursed, away from the Christ, on behalf of my brothers.” After the last verse of chapter 8 (“nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from the love of God”), chapter 9 opens…

item.title: Romans 6
item.description: “Shall we remain in sin, so that grace may increase?” The objection is built from the last verse of chapter 5, in the very verb of “where sin increased,” and Paul answers it with a fact before an order: “we who died to sin,” baptized “into his death,” “buried with him,”…

item.title: Romans 5
item.description: “Having been justified, then, out of faith, we have peace with God” — or “let us have,” since one vowel in the manuscripts turns the statement into an exhortation. ⚠ The first half is a chain: we boast in tribulation, because tribulation works out endurance, endurance proven…

item.title: Acts 28
item.description: Brought safely through, the party learns that the island is called Malta, and the barbarians show extraordinary kindness, kindling a fire; when Paul puts brushwood on it a viper fastens on his hand. ⚠ The islanders call him a murderer whom Justice has not allowed to live…

item.title: Acts 27
item.description: Paul and certain other prisoners are handed over to a centurion named Julius of the Augustan cohort, and ‘we’ set sail in a ship of Adramyttium with Aristarchus; at Sidon Julius treats Paul with kindness, and at Myra he puts the party on a ship of Alexandria bound for Italy.…

item.title: Acts 26
item.description: Agrippa tells Paul he may speak for himself, and Paul, stretching out his hand, says he counts himself happy to defend himself before a king who is an expert in the customs and questions of the Jews. ⚠ The road to Damascus is told a third time, with details the first two…

item.title: Acts 25
item.description: Festus, having entered the province, goes up after three days to Jerusalem, where the chief priests and the leading men give information against Paul and ask a favor against him — that he be sent for to Jerusalem, while they make an ambush to kill him on the way; Festus…

item.title: Acts 24
item.description: After five days the high priest Ananias comes down with some elders and an orator, Tertullus, who opens with praise for Felix’s ‘peace’ and ‘reforms’ and then calls Paul a plague, a stirrer-up of dissensions throughout the inhabited world and a ringleader of ‘the party of the…
